tasks.statement_en:
The value of the expression $x^2-6x+9$ for $x=\sqrt{3}+3$ is equal to

A. $1$
B. $3$
C. $1+2\sqrt{3}$
D. $1-2\sqrt{3}$

tasks.notes: Correct option is an enormous exact integer (~3.744e18); value given as exact JS number though double precision beyond 2^53 rounds slightly. [full-verify] Answer 2^30*3^20 (C, key X: C) is a 19-digit integer beyond 2^53: not typeable, stored float loses precision.

tasks.statement_en:
Information for tasks 7-9. The quadratic function $f$ is given by $f(x)=a(x-1)(x-3)$. The figure shows a fragment of the parabola that is the graph of this function. The vertex of this parabola is the point $W=(2,1)$.

The coefficient $a$ in the formula of function $f$ is equal to

A. $1$
B. $2$
C. $-2$
D. $-1$
tasks.notes: [verified: ok: f(2)=a(1)(-1)=-a=1 -> a=-1, option D, key D (Wersja X).]

tasks.statement_en:
Information for tasks 7-9. The quadratic function $f$ is given by $f(x)=a(x-1)(x-3)$. The figure shows a fragment of the parabola that is the graph of this function. The vertex of this parabola is the point $W=(2,1)$.

The largest value of function $f$ on the interval $\langle1,4\rangle$ is equal to

tasks.statement_en:
The equation $x(x-2)=(x-2)^2$ in the set of real numbers

A. has no solutions.
B. has exactly one solution: $x=2$.
C. has exactly one solution: $x=0$.
D. has two different solutions: $x=1$ and $x=2$.
tasks.notes: Equation simplifies to 2(x-2)=0, so x=2 is the only solution.
Options give relations between coefficients (a+b>0, a*b<0, etc.), not a specific numeric value.

tasks.statement_en:
Function $f$ is defined by the formula $f(x)=4^{-x}+1$ for every real number $x$. The number $f\left(\frac12\right)$ is equal to

A. $\frac12$
B. $\frac32$
C. $3$
D. $17$

The lines with equations $y=(m-2)x$ and $y=\frac34x+7$ are parallel. Then

A. $m=-\frac54$
B. $m=\frac23$
C. $m=\frac{11}{4}$
D. $m=\frac{10}{3}$

The sequence $(a_n)$ is defined by the formula $a_n=2n^2$ for $n\ge1$. The difference $a_5-a_4$ is equal to

A. $4$
B. $20$
C. $36$
D. $18$

In the arithmetic sequence $(a_n)$, defined for $n\ge1$, the fourth term equals $3$, and the common difference of this sequence equals $5$. The sum $a_1+a_2+a_3+a_4$ is equal to

A. $-42$
B. $-36$
C. $-18$
D. $6$

Point $A=\left(\frac13,-1\right)$ belongs to the graph of linear function $f$ defined by the formula $f(x)=3x+b$. It follows that

A. $b=2$
B. $b=1$
C. $b=-1$
D. $b=-2$

Points $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ lie on a circle with center at point $O$. The central angle $DOC$ has measure $118^\circ$ (see figure).

The measure of angle $ABC$ is equal to

A. $59^\circ$
B. $48^\circ$
C. $62^\circ$
D. $31^\circ$
tasks.notes: BC and AD are diameters; angle AOC=180-118=62 deg is the central angle for arc AC not containing B, so inscribed angle ABC = 31 deg.
Correct option is an equation of a line, not a single numeric value.
Correct option is a symbolic expression (cos alpha), valid for any acute alpha, not a specific number.

tasks.statement_en: A symmetric six-sided die, whose faces each show a different number of pips from one to six, is rolled twice. Calculate the probability of event $A$: at least one roll shows the face with five pips.
tasks.notes: P(A) = 1-(5/6)^2 = 11/36, matches key exactly.

tasks.statement_en: Angle $\alpha$ is acute and satisfies the condition $\dfrac{2\sin\alpha+3\cos\alpha}{\cos\alpha}=4$. Calculate the tangent of angle $\alpha$.
tasks.notes: Dividing gives 2 tan alpha + 3 = 4, so tan alpha = 1/2.

tasks.statement_en: Square $ABCD$ is given, in which $A=\left(5,-\frac53\right)$. Diagonal $BD$ of this square is contained in the line with equation $y=\frac43x$. Calculate the coordinates of the intersection point of diagonals $AC$ and $BD$, and the area of square $ABCD$. (sum of the intersection point's coordinates and the area)
tasks.notes: Intersection point O=(1,4/3), area=50 (verified against official key exactly). Value = 1+4/3+50 = 157/3.

tasks.statement_en: All terms of geometric sequence $(a_n)$, defined for $n\ge1$, are positive. The terms of this sequence satisfy the condition $6a_1-5a_2+a_3=0$. Calculate the ratio $q$ of this sequence belonging to the interval $\langle2\sqrt2,3\sqrt2\rangle$.
tasks.notes: q^2-5q+6=0 gives q=2 or q=3; only q=3 lies in [2sqrt2,3sqrt2]≈[2.83,4.24]. [verified: ok: q^2-5q+6=0 gives q=2 or q=3; only q=3 lies in <2sqrt2,3sqrt2> (2.83..4.24). Matches key.]

tasks.statement_en: A right square pyramid $ABCDS$ is given, whose lateral edge has length $6$ (see figure). A lateral face of this pyramid is inclined to the plane of the base at an angle whose tangent is $\sqrt7$. Calculate the volume of this pyramid.
tasks.notes: Base edge a=4, height h=2sqrt7, V=(1/3)*16*2sqrt7=32sqrt7/3; matches official key exactly.
